root_cause.text: In the erofs file-backed I/O completion handler `erofs_fileio_ki_complete`, when a read request returns fewer bytes than requested (including zero) due to reaching the end of the backing file, the remaining part of the bio was not zero-filled, leading to potential data exposure or corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `if (ret > 0)` to `if (ret >= 0 && ret != rq->bio.bi_iter.bi_size)`, ensuring that zero-filling occurs even when `ret == 0` (i.e., when the read starts at or beyond the end of the backing file). The CVE description explicitly states that "I/O requests beyond the end of the filesystem should be zeroed out, similar to loopback devices".
